items.summary: Sensory processing is fundamentally shaped by stimulation history. For example, in visual cortex, neural responses are reduced for repeated or sustained stimuli (adaptation). items.title: Quantum neuromorphic computing: harnessing noise and adaptation for scalable quantum processors
items.summary: The von Neumann bottleneck and qubit fragility limit scalable computation. items.summary: ABSTRACT Background Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder. PD currently lacks effective disease-modifying treatments, likely due to its diverse clinical features and underlying neuropathology. items.title: From Insulin Resistance to Mitochondrial Failure: A Staged Model of Impaired Metabolic Flexibility in Schizophrenia
items.summary: Schizophrenia is a highly heritable neuropsychiatric disorder whose pathophysiology remains poorly understood. While neurotransmitter, neurodevelopmental, synaptic, and dysconnectivity hypotheses explain important aspects of the disorder, growing evidence suggests that metabolic dysfunction also plays a central role. items.title: Microplastics as Emerging Neurotoxins: Brain Accumulation, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration Risk
items.summary: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) have emerged as ubiquitous environmental contaminants with profound implications for human neurological health. items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. items.title: Empathy as ontological orientation: Embodiment, therapeutic presence and mirror‐touch synaesthesia
items.summary: Abstract Empathy is widely regarded as a foundational element of effective psychotherapy and is routinely framed as a core clinical skill within training and accreditation frameworks. items.title: What Is Reasoning? A Criterion by Which Reasoning Can Be Established
items.summary: This paper examines a foundational question: What is reasoning? Across philosophy, psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence, reasoning is commonly discussed through inference, deduction, induction, abduction, deliberation, problem solving, judgment, and the drawing of conclusions. These approaches provide substantial knowledge about the forms, mechanisms, standards, and performance of reasoning, but they do not all address the same question. items.title: Deep learning without weight symmetry
items.summary: Abstract Backpropagation, a foundational algorithm for training artificial neural networks, predominates in contemporary deep learning. Although highly successful, it is widely considered biologically implausible, because it relies on precise symmetry between feedforward and feedback weights to accurately propagate gradient signals that assign credit. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. Image processing with ImageJ
items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience. ImageJ is in the public domain and runs on any operating system (OS). ImageJ is easy to use and can do many imaging manipulations. A very large and knowledgeable group makes up the user community for ImageJ. Topics covered are imaging abilities; cross platform; image formats support as of June 2004; extensions, including macros and plug-ins; and imaging library. NIH report
